verses.text: Solomon decided to build a temple to honour the LORD's name, and a royal palace for himself.
He chose seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand men to cut stone in the hills, and three thousand six hundred men to be in charge of them.
Solomon sent this message to Huram king of Tyre: "Send me cedar logs, as you did for my father David when he built his palace to live in.

I am about to build a temple to honour the name of the LORD my God and to set it apart for him. There we will burn sweet-smelling incense before him, set out the holy bread regularly, and offer burnt offerings every morning and evening, on Sabbaths, at New Moon festivals, and at the appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is a law for Israel forever.
The temple I am building will be great, because our God is greater than all gods.
But who is able to build a house for him, when even the highest heavens cannot hold him? Who am I to build a house for him, except as a place to burn incense before him?

So send me a man who is skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and with purple, red, and blue cloth, and who knows how to carve designs. He will work with the skilled craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem whom my father David provided.
Also send me cedar, pine, and algum logs from Lebanon, because I know your workers are skilled at cutting trees there. My workers will work with yours
to prepare a large amount of wood for me, because the temple I am building will be great and wonderful.
I will give your workers who cut the trees twenty thousand measures of ground wheat, twenty thousand measures of barley, twenty thousand measures of wine, and twenty thousand measures of olive oil."
Huram king of Tyre answered Solomon in a letter: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king."

Huram went on, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son, full of good sense and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a palace for himself.
I am sending you a skilled man with great understanding named Huram-Abi.

His mother was from the tribe of Dan, and his father was from Tyre. He knows how to work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and with purple, blue, and red cloth and fine linen. He can carve any kind of design and make anything that is planned for him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my master, your father David.
Now let my master send his servants the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine he promised.
We will cut all the logs you need from Lebanon and float them as rafts by sea to Joppa. Then you can take them up to Jerusalem."
Solomon counted all the foreigners living in Israel, as his father David had done before. There were one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred of them.
He made seventy thousand of them carry loads and eighty thousand cut stone in the hills. He put three thousand six hundred of them in charge, to keep the people working.
